title: Tissue-Engineered Graft for Circumferential Esophageal Reconstruction in Rats
protocol: Prepare a 20% (w/v) solution of polyurethane polymer by stirring in N,N-dimethylformamide for 8 h at room temperature.
Place the polyurethane solution on the syringe with a blunt metal needle and electrospin on rotating stainless steel mandrels at a distance of 30 cm between the needle tip and the collector.
Set the power supply to a high-voltage direct current of 15 kV potential.
Fix the feeding rate of the solution at 0.5 mL/h using a syringe pump.
Make a tubular nanofiber layer on the surface of the mandrel rotating at 3.14 m/s.
Dry the polyurethane nanofiber in a vacuum oven at 40 °C overnight to completely remove residual solvent.
Dissolve PCL pellets at 100 °C in a heating cylinder.
Print the dissolved PCL on the surface of nanofibers under high pressure (7 bar).
Remove the two-layered scaffold from the mandrel.
Sterilize the scaffold by soaking it in 70% ethanol.
Expose the scaffold to ultraviolet light for sterilization.
Soak the scaffold in 70% ethanol for 10 minutes.
Wash the scaffold three times with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Culture and expand hMSCs in growth medium.
Transfer two-layered tubular scaffolds into nonadherent 24 well tissue culture plates.
Add an hMSC suspension at a density of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL to the inner surface of the scaffold.
Uniformly deposit basement membrane matrix containing the growth medium on the inner surface.
Firmly fix the hMSC-seeded tubular scaffold to the acrylic holder in the bioreactor using a pulsatile flow system.
Add growth medium to the culture chamber in the bioreactor system.
Apply 0.1 dyne/cm² flow-induced shear stress under a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO₂.
Allow resting time of 1-2 min after applying shear stress.
Determine cell responses on inner surfaces of two-layered tubular scaffolds without bioreactor cultivation after 5 days using LIVE/DEAD Viability Assay Kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Obtain images via confocal microscopy using the Z-stack tool.
Observe surface morphology of hMSC-seeded tubular scaffold through scanning electron microscope (SEM) on the third day.
Fix scaffold incubated with hMSC with 2.5% glutaraldehyde and OsO4 for 24 hours.
Dehydrate fixed hMSCs with ethanol.
Coat fixed hMSCs with platinum using sputter coater under argon atmospheric conditions.
Obtain SEM images at an accelerating voltage of 25 kV.
Set up sterile surgical instruments.
Anesthetize the animal with an intramuscular injection of tiletamine/zolazepam (50 mg/g dose) and 2% xylazine hydrochloride (2 mg/kg dose).
Check the appropriate anesthetic condition by pinching the tail with forceps.
Place the animal in a supine position on the sterile drape.
Remove hair from the neck or abdomen using clippers.
Scrub the surgical site with betadine and 70% ethanol.
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine (0.05-0.1 mg/kg) for pain relief.
Make a midline incision of the skin and abdominal muscles to expose the stomach.
Perform gastrostomy surgery using a T-tube in rats.
Create a 3 mm orifice in the anterior gastric wall with a scalpel blade.
Insert the tip of the silicone T-tube into the defect site to fix it to the stomach wall.
Suture properly so that the T-tube does not detach from the gastric wall.
Take out the distal end of the implanted T-tube through the subcutaneous tunnel into the back of the neck.
Insert the heparin cap to the end of the T-tube to prevent the stomach contents from flowing backwards.
Suture all layers of the abdominal wall and skin using 4-0 polyglactin sutures.
Remove the neck hair of the model animals.
Perform standard draping of the surgical site for aseptic surgery.
Make an anterior median incision of the neck.
Separate the strap muscles.
Expose the tracheoesophageal structure.
Bluntly dissect the vagus nerve from the esophagus.
Resect the segment of the esophagus.
Under magnification, isolate the left side of the esophagus from the trachea.
Separate the upper part of the esophagus from the thyroid gland carefully.
Create a 5 mm long full circumferential defect containing all layers of the esophagus using surgical scissors.
Cut the prepared scaffolds to match the length of the transplant site.
Under a microscope, perform microanastomosis at both ends of the distal esophageal defect using a 9-0 suture thread.
Place the first suture between the right inferoposterior margin of the upper esophagus remnant and scaffold.
Continue suturing from right to left between the upper esophagus remnant and the scaffold.
Anastomose the scaffold in the same manner as the upper margin of the lower esophagus remnant.
Perform microvascular anastomosis for precise, watertight suturing of the implant site.
Lay the surrounding thyroid gland flap over the transplanted site to ensure stable maintenance and vascular supply to the grafts.
Stitch the subcutaneous muscle and skin tissue with a 4-0 vicryl suture.
Put rats into individual metabolic cages after surgery.
Place the cages on infrared warming devices to prevent hypothermia.
Monitor animals until they achieve and maintain sternal recumbency.
Administer gentamicin (20 mg/kg) daily to minimize inflammation at the surgical site.
Begin oral liquid feeding on the third postoperative day.
Supply whole nutrition formula through the heparin cap 3x per day beginning the day after surgery.
Check animals' appearance and body weight daily.
Manage behavior such as self-harming incision sites or resistance to tube intake.
Check for various surgical complications regularly.
Perform euthanasia by CO2 inhalation if body weight decreases rapidly by 20% or more.
Extract esophageal tissue using surgical scissors after euthanizing animals.
Perform hematoxylin and eosin staining on the extracted tissue.
Perform Masson's trichrome staining on the extracted tissue.
Conduct immunohistochemistry according to the specified protocol.
Fix the whole esophagus containing the transplanted sites in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Create a paraffin block and cut 4 µm thick sections.
Deparaffinize the tissue sections and dehydrate them in an ethanol series.
Immerse the tissue slides in citrate buffer and heat for 10 min in the microwave.
Cool the cells with cold PBS for 20 min.
Immerse in 3% hydrogen peroxide for 6 min, and wash with PBS for 10 min.
Incubate in 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA) for 1 h at room temperature to block nonspecific reactions of tissue sections.
Wash 3x with PBS for 5 min.
Incubate with primary antibodies against Desmin (diluted to 1:200), keratin 13 (diluted to 1:100), and von Willebrand Factor (vWF; diluted to 1:100) overnight at 4 °C.
Wash 3x with PBS for 15 min.
Incubate with the appropriate secondary antibody at a concentration of 1:500 for Desmin and Keratin 13 at room temperature.
Then, wash the slides twice with PBS for 10 min.
Incubate tissue sections for vWF using a horseradish peroxidase-conjugated kit and then visualize using 3,3'-diaminobenzidine (DAB).
Mount using a glass coverslip and 4',6-diamidino-2-phenolindole (DAPI) containing mounting medium.
